text:
maria: Heads up — after publishing js-sdk v2.1.0 we started getting onboarding reports: sample apps deployed to Vercel Edge fail with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED. Also a few Node14 customers report require() failures.

jon: Which change in v2.1.0 triggered it? Did we remove a compatibility field? :eyes:

maria: We switched to a stricter conditional exports map and removed the legacy main/module fields to be tidy. The exports block looks fine for modern ESM consumers but some bundlers/edge runtimes and older Node require paths that aren't covered. :confused:

sam: Vercel/esbuild often hits `Error: Package subpath './package.json' is not defined by "exports"` when package.json doesn't export package.json or when subpath imports are used. Edge runtimes also have different resolution semantics for conditional exports. Repro log: ```Error: Error: Cannot find module 'redwood-inference'
at Object.resolve (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:...)
Caused by: Error: Package subpath './package.json' is not defined by "exports"````

kevin: I can repro locally with Node 14 + require('redwood-inference'). It bails unless package.json has a main pointing at CJS. Customers on older Node hit this.

jon: Short-term fix: re-add compatibility fields. Example patch for package.json: ```json
{
  "main": "dist/cjs/index.js",
  "module": "dist/esm/index.js",
  "types": "dist/types/index.d.ts",
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
      "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
    },
    "./package.json": "./package.json"
  }
}
```
This gives most bundlers the fallback they expect and explicitly exports package.json for tools that read it.

natalie: Can we cut 2.1.1 with that patch? Onboarding is blocked for a partner. We should also add a short note in the changelog explaining the compatibility regression and recommended fixes.

maria: I'll open the patch PR now, include the package.json changes + small test harness that builds our sample app with vercel builder and runs a tiny smoke test. Kevin, can you run the Node14 compatibility check in CI?

kevin: On it — I'll add a matrix entry to our CI: node 14, 16, 18 + vercel-preview build. Running locally now.

jon: Longer term we need a CI job that verifies conditional exports across edge/bundler/resolution cases. Also consider preserving 'main'/'module' indefinitely for compatibility — the latest JS ecosystem is messy and removing legacy fields causes customer pain.

maria: Agreed. Also updating our SDK migration guide: call out that changing package exports can break bundlers and edge runtimes, and provide a minimal compatibility package.json snippet.

deploy-bot: Release candidate 2.1.1 built (rc.1) — CI passed (unit + smoke). :rocket:

maria: Awesome. Once QA signs off we'll promote. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

sam: One extra note — if we keep conditional exports, add explicit subpath exports for any internal imports our sample apps use (e.g., "./lib/*") or make sure we never require internal subpaths in examples. That prevented a bunch of silent breakages.

jon: Good call. I'll audit examples and sample apps for bare subpath requires and fix them in a follow-up.

maria: Filing follow-ups: PR for patch (opened), CI matrix addition (kevin), sample app audit (jon), docs note (maria).
